---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/wire.md, gateway/specs/endpoints/wire.schema.json, gateway/specs/endpoints/metrics.schema.json, gateway/specs/worlds/wire-codex.json, gateway/tests/fixtures/wire-codex.json, gateway/tests/test_wire_probe.py, gateway/tests/test_wire_record.py, gateway/src/agent_gateway/wire.py
Base: goal/3300-wire-record
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3300
Class: build

---
## Deliverable
A declarations file — its own file, read from the path `GATEWAY_WIRE` names — declares a GET of a vendor endpoint the gateway does not call yet, read on a schedule through the rail's own credential lifecycle and recorded as an `account` source, and names the keys whose string values that source keeps verbatim.

Island: gateway. Child of Goal #3300; lands after the recorder child (native `blockedBy`). The Goal's pin binds this issue (operator, 2026-11-12: "4 my read"): no probe and no allowlisted key is declared in the policy or in code — only in the declarations file, whose deployed copy is a codeowner path.

## Acceptance
1. `GW-WIRE-PROBE` exists on `gateway/specs/endpoints/wire.md` (section, interface row, index row, flow node) and in the `gateway/specs/README.md` index; `wire.schema.json` names the declarations file's shape (`$defs.wire_declarations`).
2. A new world file `gateway/specs/worlds/wire-codex.json` (and its byte-identical twin `gateway/tests/fixtures/wire-codex.json`) declares one probe, `codex-models`; the policy worlds are unchanged.
3. The probe rows and the allowlist rows below pass, grown to the boundary rows the pinned process asks for.
4. `gateway_wire_probe_total{source, outcome}` is in `metrics.schema.json`; `source` takes only names the file declares.
5. The fake `/models` answer is an obviously synthetic body: the probe treats bytes as opaque, and no row here asserts the vendor's shape.
6. No file outside `gateway/**` changes: the deployed `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/wire.json`, its mount and `CODEOWNERS` are not this issue's.

## Spec changes
Requirement: `GW-WIRE-PROBE` on `specs/endpoints/wire.md` — world `policy-codex` with the declarations world `wire-codex`: probe `codex-models` = rail `codex`, path `/models`, query `client_version=0.155.0`, interval 21600 s.

#### A declared probe is read

| description | declarations | lifecycle | at | request? | outcome? | recorded_class? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a declared probe goes out through the rail's lifecycle | wire-codex | a valid credential | T0 | `GET {CODEX_UPSTREAM}/models?client_version=0.155.0`, `Bearer <the lifecycle's access token>`, `chatgpt-account-id` | ok | account |
| no file, nothing read ⚖ | `GATEWAY_WIRE` unset | a valid credential | T0 | none | — | — |
| an empty file, nothing read | `{}` | a valid credential | T0 | none | — | — |
| no usable credential, no fetch ⚖ | wire-codex | the lifecycle refuses | T0 | none | no-credential | — |
| an upstream error is counted and recorded as the failure | wire-codex, the fake answers 503 | a valid credential | T0 | as the first row | fetch-failed | account |
| a restart inside the interval probes nothing at start | wire-codex, a record at T0 | a valid credential | restart at T0 + 3600 s | none | — | account |

#### What a probe may be

| description | probe | load? |
|---|---|---|
| a probe is a GET on a declared rail's upstream ⚖ | rail `codex`, path `/models` | loads |
| a rail the policy does not declare refuses the load | rail `zen`, path `/models` | refused, naming the rail |
| an absolute URL refuses the load ⚖ | path `https://elsewhere.test/models` | refused, naming path |
| an inference path refuses the load ⚖ | path `/responses` | refused, naming path |
| a method is not a key | `method: POST` | refused, naming method |

#### The declarations have one home

| description | where it is declared | load? |
|---|---|---|
| a probe in the declarations file loads | the file `GATEWAY_WIRE` names | loads |
| a `wire` key in the policy refuses the load ⚖ | `policy.json`, key `wire` | refused, naming wire |

Requirement: `GW-WIRE-RECORD` on `specs/endpoints/wire.md` — world `policy-codex`, declarations as the row says.

#### The account class's allowlist

| description | keep_keys | answer | stored? | load? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| an allowlisted key keeps its string, every other string its length ⚖ | `[slug]` | `{"slug": "fixture-model", "note": "hello"}` | `"slug": "fixture-model"`, `"note": {"len": 5}` | loads |
| no allowlist keeps no string | `[]` | the same | both strings as lengths | loads |
| no declarations file keeps no string ⚖ | `GATEWAY_WIRE` unset, source codex-usage | the observed usage shape | every string as its length | — |
| an identity key can never be allowlisted ⚖ | `[email]` | — | — | refused, naming email |
| an allowlisted value that matches a credential pattern is still withheld ⚖ | `[slug]` | `{"slug": "sk-ant-oat-FAKE…"}` | withheld | loads |

Index row: new — `GW-WIRE-PROBE | the declared probe | —`.
Unverified: the identity-key set (`email`, `account_id`, `user_id`, anything token- or cookie-named are the floor — the usage payload's identity fields are the one observed case); whether `chatgpt-account-id` is needed on `/models` (the 2026-10-29 hand probe went through `responses.upstream_headers`); the module that loads the file (not in `Touches` — name it in the PR); a malformed declarations file at start — ⚖ refuse to start, like a malformed policy, is the proposal; the real `/models` shape is NOT this issue's — it is what the deployed probe will record.

## Out of scope
- `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/wire.json`, the Deployment's mount and env, `CODEOWNERS` — the Goal's post-launch leg and the seat's hand.
- `GW-CATALOG-CODEX` (#3296): parsing or serving the account's model list.
- A probe on any rail other than a declared one, a non-GET probe, a probe that carries a body.
title: gateway: GW-WIRE-PROBE — a declared read of a vendor endpoint the gateway does not call yet, and the account class's key allowlist

---
Touches: gateway/scripts/wire-quarry.py, gateway/tests/test_wire_quarry.py, gateway/specs/endpoints/wire.md, gateway/specs/worlds/README.md, gateway/devbox.json
Base: goal/3300-wire-record
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3300
Class: build

---
## Deliverable
`gateway/scripts/wire-quarry.py` — a stdlib tool that reads the gateway's wire door and prints a recorded answer with its provenance, finds which source has a shape, and cuts a fragment into a fixture file with a provenance sidecar; `gateway/specs/worlds/README.md` says where worlds come from.

Island: gateway. Child of Goal #3300; lands after the recorder child (native `blockedBy`).

## Acceptance
1. `GW-WIRE-QUARRY` exists on `gateway/specs/endpoints/wire.md` (section, index row, flow node) and in the `gateway/specs/README.md` index; the rows below pass against an in-process door, grown to the boundary rows the pinned process asks for.
2. The tool imports the standard library only and takes the door's base URL from the environment (default: the cluster Service name) — it holds and sends no credential.
3. `devbox run wire-quarry -- <verb>` exists in `gateway/devbox.json`.
4. `gateway/specs/worlds/README.md` gains §Where worlds come from: a fixture is cut from a recorded answer with `wire-quarry.py cut`, its sidecar is committed beside it, and a shape no source has recorded is not written.
5. `GW-WIRE-QUARRY`'s index row carries `⚑ gap`: the fixtures cut by hand before this tool have no sidecar, and nothing lints for one.

## Spec changes
Requirement: `GW-WIRE-QUARRY` on `specs/endpoints/wire.md` — world `policy-codex`, the door holding `go-models-dev` (the `catalog-ok` bytes, T0).

#### Reading the door

| description | door | command | exit? | stdout? | stderr? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `show` prints one member verbatim and one provenance line | go-models-dev at T0 | `show go-models-dev` | 0 | the stored bytes, byte-identical | `wire: source=go-models-dev class=public sha256=<…> fetched_at=T0` |
| `list` prints the index | go-models-dev at T0 | `list` | 0 | one line per source: name, class, status, age | — |
| `find` names the sources that have a key, with its path ⚖ | go-models-dev at T0 | `find --key cost` | 0 | `go-models-dev` and each JSON path ending in `cost` | — |
| a source nobody recorded is an error, never an empty answer | go-models-dev at T0 | `show codex-models` | 4 | nothing | `wire: codex-models not recorded` |
| a silent door is an error that names the door ⚖ | unreachable | `show go-models-dev` | 3 | nothing | `wire: door unreachable: <url>` |

#### Cutting a fixture

| description | door | command | exit? | fixture? | sidecar? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cut` writes the fragment's values unchanged and a sidecar ⚖ | go-models-dev at T0 | `cut go-models-dev --path opencode-go.models.deepseek-v4-pro --out <dir>/m.json` | 0 | that subtree, values and key order as recorded | `<dir>/m.provenance.json`: source, class, url, sha256 of the whole answer, fetched_at, path |
| a path the answer does not have writes nothing | go-models-dev at T0 | `cut go-models-dev --path opencode-go.models.nope --out <dir>/m.json` | 5 | no file | no file |
| a truncated record is never cut | go-models-dev, `complete: false` | `cut go-models-dev --path opencode-go --out <dir>/m.json` | 6 | no file | no file |
| a silent door writes nothing | unreachable | `cut go-models-dev --path opencode-go --out <dir>/m.json` | 3 | no file | no file |

Index row: new — `GW-WIRE-QUARRY | the quarry tool | ⚑ gap (<the PR's date>, PR #<this PR> → work #<the successor the PR names>): fixtures cut before the tool carry no provenance sidecar; no lint requires one`.
Unverified: the exit codes and the sidecar's file name are proposals (⚖ a sidecar keeps the fixture's bytes the vendor's; a wrapper key would not); how a non-JSON member (the Go page, `go.mdx`) is cut — `show` covers it, `cut --path` is JSON-only unless the implementation finds a better seam; the env name for the door's URL.

## Out of scope
- Re-cutting or re-dating the existing fixtures under `gateway/tests/fixtures/`.
- A provenance lint in `spec_gate.py` or `ci.sh`.
- `.agents/fix.yaml` — the worker recipe's use of this tool is the agent-loop island's.
- Any write to the door, the store, the policy or the declarations file.
title: gateway: GW-WIRE-QUARRY — wire-quarry.py reads the wire door and cuts a fixture with its provenance; worlds/README says where worlds come from

---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md, gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.schema.json, gateway/specs/worlds/README.md, gateway/tests/test_tiers_runtime.py, gateway/README.md, gateway/src/agent_gateway/
Base: goal/3305-runtime-tiers
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3305
Class: build

---
## Deliverable
The gateway derives the per-(rail, tier) model lists from its own store at each catalog refresh, keeps the last good derivation, and shows it on `GET /catalog/tiers` beside the list the admission walks — the admission itself is untouched.

Island: gateway. Second child of the runtime-tiers Goal (the shadow step). The operator's ruling (2026-11-12): "I am also leaning towards runtime. But with some monitoring, S3, grafana, etc. Can all be added later when it works already."

## Acceptance
1. `GW-MODEL-TIERS` on `gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md` gains the section and key rows below; the derivation is `agent_gateway.tiers`' own (`derive`, `join_aa_id`, `cost_per_clean_ride`, `undecided`, `unscored`) — no rule of it changes, and every existing GW-MODEL-TIERS row still passes.
2. A derivation runs after every good refresh of either catalog leg, from: the benched rows (`GET /catalog/openrouter` `benchmarks`, the first child), the Go price (`GET /catalog/opencode` `pricing`), the openrouter models' selected endpoints and rides, the manual benchmark rows when a file is mounted, and the policy's `tiers` block.
3. Candidates per rail ⚖: `opencode` and `openrouter` as GW-MODEL-TIERS §The rulings state them (from the two catalogs); `anthropic` and `codex` = the ids of the policy's `rails.<rail>.models` lists. No upstream read on a subscription credential is added.
4. `GET /catalog/tiers` answers a shape `catalog.schema.json` names: `derived_at`, the evidence stamps (the benched set's `as_of`, the two catalogs' `fetched_at`), and per rail and tier the derived list, each id's evidence row (score, price, basis, rides), `undecided`, `unscored`, and `equals_walked`.
5. The last good derivation is stored and survives a restart; a refresh whose derivation cannot run (no benched rows) keeps it.
6. The manual rows keep their rule: a row scores only an id the feed lacks, a row the feed carries is reported retired on the view; a malformed file refuses the whole file and the derivation runs without it ⚖.

## Spec changes
Requirement: `GW-MODEL-TIERS` on `specs/endpoints/catalog.md` — world `policy-default` · `openrouter-endpoints` with the Go catalog (`catalog-ok` + `docs-ok`) and the openrouter-catalog world's benched rows.

#### The derivation at a refresh

| description | store_before | refresh | derived_at? | lists? | equals_walked? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a good refresh derives every rail's tiers ⚖ | catalogs and benched rows at T0, no derivation | openrouter leg ok at T0 + 21600 s | T0 + 21600 s | per rail and tier what `derive` returns over the store's evidence | per tier, true where the policy's list is the same ids in the same order |
| the feed moves, the lists move with no commit ⚖ | a derivation at T0 | the benched rows change one candidate's `intelligence` across a band | the refresh's time | the candidate enters or leaves the tier as the band says | false on that tier |
| a tier with no priced candidate is undecided and keeps its last derived list ⚖ | a derivation at T0 with openrouter `light` decided | every openrouter price null | the refresh's time | openrouter `light`: the T0 list, named under `undecided` | — |
| a benched candidate with no value on the score axis is in no list and is named ⚖ | catalogs at T0 | a candidate row with `intelligence` null | the refresh's time | absent from every tier, present in `unscored` | — |
| a subscription rail's candidates are the policy's ids ⚖ | policy `rails.anthropic.models` naming four aliases | ok | the refresh's time | anthropic tiers hold only those aliases, score ascending | — |

#### What a failed input leaves

| description | store_before | refresh | derived_at? | lists? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no benched rows, no derivation | empty store | openrouter leg fetch-failed | none | none on any rail |
| a failed refresh keeps the last good derivation | a derivation at T0 | openrouter leg fetch-failed at T0 + 21600 s | T0 | the T0 lists |
| one rail's input missing holds that rail only ⚖ | benched rows present, no Go catalog | ok | the refresh's time | opencode: none; the other rails derived |
| the derivation survives a restart | a derivation at T0 | none (restart at T0 + 3600 s) | T0 | the T0 lists |

#### The view's shape (tiers)

| description | store | shape? |
|---|---|---|
| the view's shape is the schema's | a derivation at T0 | exactly the schema's required keys |
| no derivation is an empty view, never an error | empty store | `derived_at` null, no rails |

Index row: no change (the "hand-refreshed" gap row stays until the last child).
Unverified (verify during implementation):
- The world: no existing world carries both the endpoint snapshot and the benched rows; ⚖ compose the two recorded sets, or seed the store — say which on the worlds page.
- How the manual rows reach the pod: ⚖ an optional file named by an environment variable (`GATEWAY_BENCHMARKS_MANUAL`), unmounted = no manual rows. Mounting `benchmarks-manual.json` is the Goal's post-launch step, not this child's.
- The alternative on `anthropic` / `codex` candidates (a policy key of their own) was not taken: the existing lists are the cheaper-to-reverse declaration.
- Whether the trigger is each leg's refresh or a tick of its own (⚖ each good refresh).

## Out of scope
- The admission: `POST /sessions` still walks the policy's lists (the next child).
- `benchmarks.json`, `benchmarks-snapshot.sh`, `tiers snapshot | apply | check` and their rows: untouched here (the last child).
- A gauge beyond the existing one, an alert, S3; anything under `argocd/`.
title: gateway: GW-MODEL-TIERS — derive the tier lists at each catalog refresh and show them on GET /catalog/tiers (admission untouched)

---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md, gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.schema.json, gateway/specs/endpoints/catalog.md, gateway/tests/test_sessions_admit.py, gateway/tests/test_tiers_runtime.py, gateway/src/agent_gateway/
Base: goal/3305-runtime-tiers
Origin: teststuffstash/homelab#3305
Class: build

---
## Deliverable
`POST /sessions` walks the derived tier lists instead of the policy's, and holds a rail that has no derivation — with none on any rail, every session defers until the first derivation completes.

Island: gateway. Third child of the runtime-tiers Goal (the cut-over). The operator's ruling (2026-11-12) on what a session walks when the gateway holds no derivation — defer every session until the first derivation completes, or keep seed lists in the policy: "2 defer".

## Acceptance
1. `GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT` on `gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md` carries the key rows below; the walk's order, overrides, harness rule, `prefer` and the rail choice are unchanged — only where a tier's list comes from changes.
2. A rail with no derivation is held with the typed defer `tiers-underived` (in `sessions.schema.json`'s defer reasons) and a `retry_after_s`; the walk moves to the role's next rail; every rail held → the answer is that defer.
3. The policy loader accepts a policy with and without `rails.opencode.models` / `rails.openrouter.models` lists; when present they order nothing. `anthropic` and `codex` lists stay required (they declare the candidates).
4. A restart on a file store dispatches from the stored derivation without waiting for a refresh; a restart on an empty or `:memory:` store defers until the first derivation.
5. `GET /catalog/tiers` `equals_walked` is true on every tier once the walk reads the derivation; the `GW-MODEL-TIERS` row that says so is added.

## Spec changes
Requirement: `GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT` on `specs/endpoints/sessions.md` — world `policy-default`, with a derivation seeded or absent as each row says. One row on `GW-MODEL-TIERS` (`specs/endpoints/catalog.md`).

#### Where a tier's list comes from

| description | world | derivation | role | tier | decision? | rail? | model? | reason? | retry_after_s? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| the walk reads the derived list, not the policy's ⚖ | policy-default | the role's first rail derived, its tier's first id differing from the policy's | worker | standard | dispatch | the role's first rail | the derived list's first id | — | — |
| no derivation anywhere: every session defers ⚖ | policy-default | none | worker | standard | defer | — | — | tiers-underived | the configured wait |
| a rail with no derivation is held, the next rail serves ⚖ | policy-default | none for the role's first rail, the second derived | worker | standard | dispatch | the role's second rail | its derived list's first id | — | — |
| an undecided tier walks its last derived list ⚖ | policy-default | the tier undecided, a last good list kept | worker | light | dispatch | that rail | the kept list's first id | — | — |
| a tier never derived on a derived rail is empty there ⚖ | policy-default | the rail derived, this tier undecided with nothing kept | worker | heavy | dispatch or defer as the role's other rails answer | the next rail | — | — | — |
| an explicit model outside the derived lists keeps its existing answer | policy-default | derived | worker, explicit model | — | as GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT's explicit-override rows say today | — | — | — | — |

#### The policy without the priced rails' lists

| description | policy | load? |
|---|---|---|
| a policy with the lists loads; they order nothing | policy-default | ok |
| a policy without `rails.opencode.models` and `rails.openrouter.models` loads ⚖ | policy-default with those two blocks removed | ok |
| a policy without `rails.anthropic.models` is refused ⚖ | policy-default with that block removed | refused, naming the key |

#### `GW-MODEL-TIERS` — the walked list is the derived one

| description | store | equals_walked? |
|---|---|---|
| after the cut-over every tier equals what the admission walks | a derivation at T0 | true on every tier |

Index row: no change.
Unverified (verify during implementation):
- `retry_after_s` for `tiers-underived`: ⚖ a fixed short wait (60 s) — the first derivation follows the first catalog refresh at start; no page states a number.
- Which requirement owns the loader's `models` shape (`GW-MODEL-RESOLVE` loads the deployed policy and checks its ids against `model-classes.json` — that row must keep passing with the priced rails' lists absent; if it reads those lists, its replacement is a ⚖ row in this PR).
- Whether a consumer treats an unknown defer reason as fatal: the launchers read `reason` (the loop's side is outside this island's read set) — name what was checked in the PR body.
- The fifth row's exact answer depends on the world's second rail; write the observed value.

## Out of scope
- Removing the lists from `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/policy.json` (the Goal's post-launch step); anything under `argocd/`.
- A seed list, a fallback to the policy's lists (ruled out).
- The rail choice between twins, `prefer`, the retry contract — unchanged.
- A new alert: the existing `TierEvidenceStale` arm on an absent gauge is the belt.
title: gateway: GW-SESSIONS-ADMIT — the walk reads the derived tier lists; no derivation defers

body:
---
Touches: gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md, gateway/specs/README.md, gateway/specs/glossary.md, gateway/tests/test_sessions_retry.py, gateway/tests/test_sessions_outcome.py, gateway/src/agent_gateway/sessions.py, gateway/src/agent_gateway/tiers.py
Origin: gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md#GW-SESSIONS-RETRY
Class: build

---
## Deliverable

The retry walk reads the twin rule it already has: a model-scoped strike on one policy id excludes that model's twins on every rail for the task, and the `⚑ gap: one model across rails is two ids` row and flags are gone.

Lineage: standalone — filed by island intake (2026-11-15) from the `⚑ gap` row of GW-SESSIONS-RETRY (`gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md` §Named gaps — retry). The row's rationale is stale: it says the per-model grouping "is not in the gateway policy", but since 2026-11-06 the gateway carries exactly that grouping as the twin rule (`same_model`, one rule, no table — GW-RAIL-CHOICE §The twin rule, glossary §twin), read by the rail choice and by nothing else. Live today (the deployed `argocd/resources/agent-gateway/policy.json`), the light tier names two twin pairs — `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` ↔ `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash` ↔ `xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash` — so a model-scoped strike on one re-admits the same model on the other rail at the task's next attempt, which is the re-dispatch rule 3 of model-routing.md says a failed attempt buys. GW-SESSIONS-OUTCOME §The vocabulary already states the rule this closes ("a model-scoped one excludes the model on every rail for the task"); GW-SESSIONS-RETRY contradicts it ("the same model on another rail is another id").

## Acceptance

1. GW-SESSIONS-RETRY carries a new sub-table **§A strike crosses the twins** (its own heading and header, directly after §Strikes walk the list — the existing table, its six rows and the proving test's argnames untouched) with the three rows under §Spec changes, each `rule("GW-SESSIONS-RETRY")`-labelled in `gateway/tests/test_sessions_retry.py` and green; the prose sentence "⚖ Model identity is the policy id: the same model on another rail is another id, so a model strike on `claude/sonnet` does not exclude `opencode-go/claude-haiku-5-5`" is rewritten to the twin reading (below), and the three base sentences under §Spec changes → Prose substitutions no longer say a model-scoped strike stops at the policy id.
2. GW-SESSIONS-OUTCOME §Refutation carries the one ⚖ row under §Spec changes, labelled in `gateway/tests/test_sessions_outcome.py` and green.
3. The gap row of §Named gaps — retry is deleted and the three index clauses are trimmed as §Spec changes names; `devbox run ci` green (spec gate, join + hygiene ratchets, lychee).
4. The PR body carries `Spec changes:` (rule 1).

## Spec changes

Requirement: `GW-SESSIONS-RETRY` on `gateway/specs/endpoints/sessions.md` — world `policy-default`; a new heading `#### A strike crosses the twins` after §Strikes walk the list, with the header below (the worker's policy tier is `standard`, so `tier` is an input here; `reason?` as §Cooled, exhausted, or held spells it, `—` on a dispatch). Legend as §Strikes walk the list's: `T` = the task; `strikes` = `class on (rail, model)` for a cell strike, `class on model` for a model strike. A worker's rails are `opencode` then `openrouter`; the light lists are `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `[deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash]`; `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` and `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` are twins (GW-RAIL-CHOICE §The twin rule, row "a Go id and its openrouter spelling are twins"). In every row one of the twins is struck for T, so no rail choice runs and the role's rail order stands (GW-RAIL-CHOICE prose: "A twin struck for the task is the retry contract's business, not the choice's (no choice; the walk skips it)") — whatever the Go cell's price in the world.

| description | world | role | tier | task | strikes | attempt | decision? | rail? | model? | reason? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| "a model strike on a twin excludes the twin on the other rail" ⚖ | policy-default | worker | light | T | no-pr on deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash | 2 | dispatch | openrouter | deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash | — |
| "a cell strike on a twin leaves the other rail's twin cell admissible" | policy-default | worker | light | T | harness-gave-up on (openrouter, deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash) | 2 | dispatch | opencode | opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash | — |

The first row's ⚖: the alternative is the status quo (two ids, the twin is the retry); the scope table already calls a model-scoped strike the model's own fault, not the cell's, so the twin — the same model under another rail's price — inherits it.
